findings.reason: without the declared edge the node can be dispatched simultaneously with §31 against the same file, which is the collision §33 names as the reason to build after it; the plan's own convention declares exactly this kind of in-plan file-sharing edge (s28→s26, s30→s28), so the omission is a gap rather than a departure from the plan's practice.
findings.text: §33 declares "Build it after §31, which also writes `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`" only in its prose, while the plan's `plan-section-depends-on` (line 21) carries no `s33→s31` edge; §31 (`s31`, implementable) and §33 both write `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, so the scheduler can dispatch them concurrently on one file and the ordering §33 requires is unenforceable

findings.reason: §33's own Why records the brief surviving the failing hold and being reused by the later direct dispatch (11:49 write, 11:50:08 reuse, report 11:59), so its "brief kept, the way a held plan review does" premise names a plan-review discard path the code-review path has no counterpart to; the author should drop the brief-keeping clause and its assertion, or restate the code review's brief as already durable, rather than send a node to build a protection against a loss that cannot occur.
findings.text: §33's first case asserts "the brief file still present", but a code review's brief is composed at a neighbourhood-keyed, non-run-scoped path (`code_review_report_directory(subject)/brief.md`, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2654-2659`) that no code path removes — unlike the plan review, whose run-scoped composed directory `_discard_composed_plan_review` deletes (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1829-1835`) — so the brief-presence assertion passes on the unfixed code and cannot show the guard fires

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited brief path `reports/reckon/code-review/a04aa9b45afb/brief.md` resolves on disk (written 11:49, sidecar `code-review.json` present), and the cited run `r-20261019T095008083939` is a completed run of that neighbourhood.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §33's done-when (line 206) asserts "the brief file still present" for the composed code review, an assertion that already holds on the unfixed code and so measures nothing.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §33 logs its reproduction and both arms under the run's report directory, with each log ending in `EXIT=`, and names `<reports>/<project>/code-review/<key>/brief.md` under the crew reports store.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §33's new symbols and comments are named by mechanism (`_LANE_GATE_WAITING_STATES`, `is_local`, `shadow_lineage` named as "shadow lineage"); no plan label, ticket, version tag or changelog prose reaches the code.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §33's stated mechanism matches the cited code: the lane-gate raise is `LanePaused(lane_gate)` built from the gate's own `detail` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1174-1179`), the quoted reason is the allowance's grant + verdict built at `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1238-1248`, the queue short-circuit is `if is_local and not shadow_lineage:` under `lane_allowance.get("held")` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1546-1547`), `is_local` compares the resolved backend with `local_backend` (`:1461`), and `local_backend: clive` is the live flight value — so the two candidates §33 enumerates (is_local false, or a shadow lineage) are the complete set that reaches `raise LaneHeld(lane_allowance)` at `:1594`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §33 carries one deliverable: a router-held composed code review on the local lane queues with its brief kept; the diagnostic step (name which of the two codepaths skipped the short-circuit) is reconnaissance for that one goal, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §33 (§33 line 206) states in §33's own prose "Build it after §31, which also writes `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`", but `plan-section-depends-on` (line 21) declares only `s28→s26` and `s30→s28`, so the scheduler cannot see the required §33-after-§31 order on that one file.
